tools.export_note: Saved in {}. Attach it to a bug report. It never contains the serial number.
tools.logs_note: Applies to the diagnostic reports, the crash files, the session logs and the links of the reports sent online in {}, each on its own, at start-up and when a limit changes. The newest one always stays.
tools.storage_emummc: A copy on the SD card (emuMMC)
tools.upload_note: Sends a report to a secret gist in your GitHub account (sign in first if needed) and shows its link with a QR code: give it to whoever helps you, or open a bug report with it.

about.support_body: PlayShelf is free, open source and has no ads. If it helps your family, you can support its development: scan a code with your phone.
about.reminder_off: The monthly reminder is off. Preferences › Notifications turns it back on.

prefs.support_reminder: Remind me once a month to support PlayShelf

update.available_no_fw: It does not support firmware {} yet.
update.no_release: No PlayShelf release is published yet: {} is a development build.
update.manual_body: To update, open sphaira (its GitHub menu already knows PlayShelf) or the Homebrew App Store, or download playshelf.nro from {} and copy it to /switch/playshelf/ on the SD card.
update.open_body: PlayShelf will close and open {}. Find PlayShelf there to update it.
update.store_behind: {} still has PlayShelf {}: it publishes {} after a review, often a few days later. PlayShelf can update itself now instead. Your settings are kept.
update.title: Update available
update.headline: PlayShelf {} is available
update.notes_none: No notes could be read for this version. All versions: {}
update.inplace_body: PlayShelf will download version {}, check it, put it in place of this one and restart on it. Your settings are kept.

upload.current: This report and the debug files
upload.confirm_gist: A secret gist in your GitHub account: anyone with the link can read it, until you delete it on GitHub. It never contains the serial number.
upload.confirm_public: A bug report opened with this link is public. Only the last changes of the history are sent, without names or times of day.
upload.relogin: GitHub refused the gist: PlayShelf's sign-in does not allow gists. Sign in again to allow them? To sign out instead: {}.
upload.needs_github: The report goes to a secret gist in your GitHub account: anyone with its link can read it, until you delete it on GitHub. PlayShelf is not signed in to GitHub yet. Sign in now?
upload.needs_github_list: The list goes to a secret gist in your GitHub account: anyone with its link can read it, until you delete it on GitHub. PlayShelf is not signed in to GitHub yet. Sign in now?
upload.done_list:
List sent

Scan the code with a phone, or open the link on a computer, to find these games again.

A copy of the link stays on the SD card, in PlayShelf's logs/uploads folder. To delete the list, sign in on gist.github.com.
upload.done:
Report sent

To report a bug, scan the code on the right. If someone is already helping you, give them the one on the left.

A copy of the link stays on the SD card, in PlayShelf's logs/uploads folder. To delete the report, sign in on gist.github.com.
upload.partial: Too large: only the start will be sent.

dev.clear_cache_body:
Delete the cache: {}?

The game names and icons and the development build list. PlayShelf fetches them again when it needs them.
dev.clear_logs_body:
Delete the log files: {}?

The crash files, the session logs (all but this run's) and the saved diagnostic reports. Kept: the links of the reports sent online (the only way to remove them).
dev.clear_failed:
Deleted: {}.

Not deleted, refused by the SD card: {}.
dev.frame_stats_note: One line every second while PlayShelf is open, in logs/frame_stats.txt: the mode (docked or handheld) and the frame size, the screen shown, the frames per second, the UI's own computing time per frame (mean and maximum, in ms), the interval between two frames (mean and maximum) and how many frames came late (more than 20 ms). To compare screens, or the background glow on and off: leave each screen shown for 30 s without touching anything, docked then handheld. The file starts over each time this is turned on.
dev.mode_off_body: Turn developer mode off? Its tools leave the end of About › Help & diagnostics and the play-timer recording stops. Seven presses of Y on About › Version bring them back.
dev.read_only_off_body: Leave read-only mode? PlayShelf can then change the console again (install, remove).
dev.enabled: Developer mode is on: see the end of About › Help & diagnostics.
dev.presses_left: {} more presses to turn on developer mode.
dev.presses_left_one: 1 more press to turn on developer mode.
